## Human review verdict — chalbert/web-everything#1488

**Verdict:** 🚩 prevention outstanding — file the guard before accept

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | prevention-outstanding |

### Findings (1)

**correctness** (1)
- `scripts/check-standards-rules.mjs:3116` — Quote state is not carried across physical lines, so an unterminated string that closes mid-way through the next physical line can make the scanner treat that whole next line as a comment, hiding a real `--all` invocation that follows the closing quote on it. — A hook containing `MSG='explanation that spans\n# multiple lines' ; node x.mjs --all` genuinely executes `node x.mjs --all` in bash (verified live: `ARGS: x.mjs --all`). `logicalLines` does not join these two physical lines (no trailing backslash), so `findGitHookAllFlags` scans line 2 (`# multiple lines' ; node x.mjs --all`) on its own with quote state reset to null. `shellCodeOf` then sees a `#` at position 0 with no open quote and treats the ENTIRE line as a comment, so `shellWords` never sees `node`, `x.mjs`, or `--all` at all. Result: `findGitHookAllFlags` returns `[]` for a hook that really does run `--all` unattended — reproduced against the exact code from the diff (extracted verbatim into a standalone file and executed with node). No named test in the added suite exercises this input; none reddens because none exists for it — this is a genuine, currently-undefended miss, not a mutation of an existing passing case. The shape is a fairly ordinary one (a multi-line single- or double-quoted string followed by more code on the line where the quote closes), not an exotic construct like a heredoc or `$IFS` trick, yet it is not named in the backlog card's explicit 'not modelled' list (which only calls out variable-assembled flags, $IFS games, heredocs and the `\-\-all`-in-double-quotes over-report) — so a reader trusts the surface is smaller than it is. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: broken]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Add a mutation-tested fixture (matching this suite's own established pattern) for an unterminated quote on one physical line that closes and is followed by a real `--all` invocation on the next physical line, and either fix `logicalLines`/`shellCodeOf` to carry quote state across physical lines or explicitl day add this shape to the backlog card's 'not modelled' list so it isn't mistaken for covered surface.

---

**Decision:** `accept` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `6d3ad31e2202e8f6052bd7fd0002c771f4d813d8..70ad49e86bf3b2e42a8245e14f51511cebfce31d` (rev `origin/lane/3196-githooks-all-flag` at review time) — 4 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

_Recorded through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035)._

> **Carve-out captured as `#x8952dw`.** The one finding — quote state not carried across physical lines — is filed with its bash-verified case rather than fixed here. This PR spent seven rounds on this detector, each closing a real form; the fix for this one is small and separable, so the six closed forms land and it is taken on its own.
